search.website_text:
Time Memoria — FFXIV quest progression and pacing. Pre-release rebuild on a generated quest data layer. # Time Memoria

A FFXIV Dalamud plugin for quest progression and pacing — a reflective notebook
for your story journey, not a scoreboard.

> ⚠️ This plugin **cannot** be used for ACT/FFLogs-style performance analysis.
> It does not track, read, or evaluate combat performance in any way.

![The Quests tab](assets/quests.png)

Browse by expansion and section, or let **Recommended** answer "what next" — the
oldest thing outstanding, the next Main Scenario quest, and the next quest for
every job you have actually unlocked. The patch each quest arrived in is not in
the game's own tables; it ships as data.

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Overview](assets/overview.png) | ![Progression](assets/progression.png) |
| Completion by expansion and by section. Excluded categories stay visible but uncounted. | Class and job levels, coloured by role, marking the least progressed in each. |

![The at-a-glance window](assets/mini.png)

A small companion window for while you are actually playing: playtime with the
age of the reading, session and lifetime pacing, and the battle jobs furthest
behind.

Every window above is drawn with the game's own widgets. There is a classic
ImGui version of all of it too — `/tm classic` — and a setting for which one
`/tm` opens.

---

## Status: released

**Time Memoria is published.** Install it by adding this repository to Dalamud's
custom plugin repositories:

```
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LegendsOfTheGame/TimeMemoriaV3/main/repo.json
```

It is also carried by [Senither's plugin
list](https://dalamud-plugins.senither.com/plugin/TimeMemoriaV3), which merges a
number of third-party repositories into a single URL.

Two earlier versions were built and flown before this one, which is why it began
at **3.0** rather than 1.0 — it is shaped by what they taught.

[TimeMemoriaV2](https://github.com/LegendsOfTheGame/TimeMemoriaV2) is kept for
reference. It maintained its quest data by hand — 288 JSON files needing an
update every patch — and that is why it stalled: patch 7.5 landed in April 2026
and the data was never added.

This version reads quest data from the game's own journal tables instead, so a
patch's content appears the day it lands and no one has to do anything. That is
the whole point of the rebuild, and it is a direct answer to how the last one
failed. Numbering it 1.0 would hide that.

### Module state

| Module | State |
|---|---|
| Quest UI | ✅ generated from journal tables |
| News / Events | ✅ feed plus client-read festivals |
| Playtime & pacing | ✅ session and lifetime |
| Class & job progression | ✅ with clipboard export |
| Patch attribution | ✅ patch column on quests and What's New |
| Native game windows | ✅ every tab, plus a companion window |
| Ocean Fishing helper | ❌ future |

### Versioning

`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.API` — releasing at **`3.0.0.15`**.

The last digit is the Dalamud API level the build targets, so you can tell which
game version a build is for without opening the manifest. It is safe in the last
position: API levels only ever climb, so the version stays monotonic, which
Dalamud requires for updates to install. Putting it *first* would make a routine
API bump look like a major release of the plugin.

Time Memoria v2 used `AA.B.C.D`, where the digits encoded API level, expansion
band, patch band, and how many quest buckets had been hand-extracted. That was
right for a plugin whose central problem was migrating quest data by hand — the
version told you how far through it you were.

This version has no buckets, and covers every expansion and patch the moment the
game does. Under the old scheme it would read `15.7.5.9` on day one and never
move again. The module table above carries what those digits used to.

### What works

- Quest data generated from the game's own journal tables — no hand-maintained
  quest files, so a patch's content appears the day it lands
- Two-panel questline tree, chain-grouped, with search across every expansion
  including ones the tree is hiding
- Suggested next quest, and per-expansion and per-category progress
- The patch each quest arrived in — not in the game files at all, so it ships
  as data
- MSQ progression gating, spoiler mode, free-trial mode
- Class and job levelling, role-coloured, with clipboard export
- Playtime pacing, session and lifetime
- World state: maintenance windows, patch status, and active events read from
  the client rather than only from the news feed
- What's New — quests added since the baseline snapshot, with the build they
  arrived in
- Per-character completion dates from first install onwards
- Help and Credits

---

## Building

Native UI comes from [KamiToolKit](https://github.com/MidoriKami/KamiToolKit),
which is not published as a package — it is a submodule, and **the build will
fail without it**:

```
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LegendsOfTheGame/TimeMemoriaV3
```

Already cloned? `git submodule update --init --recursive`, then:

```
dotnet build TimeMemoria.csproj
```

Requires the .NET 10 SDK and a Dalamud development environment.

The assembly is named `TimeMemoriaV3` permanently. Dalamud derives InternalName
from it, and InternalName keys the configuration file and the directory holding
the quest journal — renaming it would orphan both. Only the display name matters
to anyone using the plugin, and that is `Time Memoria`.

---

## Credits

Time Memoria's quest data layer derives from **QuestTracker**, originally by
[isaiahcat](https://github.com/isaiahcat/QuestTracker) and currently maintained
by [keifufu](https://github.com/keifufu/QuestTracker), used under AGPL-3.0. It
is an independent plugin, not affiliated with or endorsed by either author.

See [NOTICE](NOTICE) for the full attribution and the list of changes.

Inspiration, though no code, also came from
[BetterPlaytime](https://github.com/caitlyn-gg/BetterPlaytime) by Infi and
Caitlyn, and [LeveHelper](https://github.com/Haselnussbomber/LeveHelper) by
Haselnussbomber.

---

## Compliance

Time Memoria is strictly a quest progression and pacing tool.

It does **not**:

- Read or display DPS, HPS, deaths, wipes, or duty results
- Integrate with ACT, FFLogs, or any combat log format
- Automate any in-game interaction
- Transmit your data anywhere — the clipboard export is local and user-initiated

Saved data is limited to quest IDs, completion counts, timestamps, pacing
aggregates, and class/job levels. Nothing it stores can be repurposed as a
combat log.

---

## AI usage

Development was AI-assisted at the **Copilot** level as defined by Dalamud's
[AI Usage Policy](https://dalamud.dev/plugin-publishing/ai-policy/) — AI
implements, the maintainer plans, tests and reviews. No assets are AI-generated.

[AI-DECLARATION.md](AI-DECLARATION.md) records this in full, including what AI
got wrong and how it was caught.

---

## Licence

[AGPL-3.0](LICENSE).

variant.changelog:
Our largest update since 3.0.

Native window - Story Remaining:
- Add Story Remaining to the Native overview. It existed only in Classic, so switching to the window being actively developed cost you the projection that most justifies the plugin.
- Reproduce Classic's wording exactly, down to the singular "quest" when one is left and the gate sentence being dropped on the final expansion.
- Move the calculation out of Classic's draw code into a shared helper both windows now call, so the two can no longer drift apart or disagree on a figure.
- Quote a single pacing figure. Story Remaining previously cited the Main Scenario rate three rows under a row showing the same number, so "28m per quest" could sit above "at your rate of 28m 16s per quest".
- Make the overview panel scroll, and raise its capacity from 26 rows to 48. At the 460px minimum window size the surplus rows did not vanish - they drew over the window's own border.
- Hide a row's whole container rather than just its text, so the scrollbar describes the rows you can actually see instead of counting hidden ones.
- Say so, once, if the row pool is ever exhausted. Silently dropping the surplus is why the old ceiling went unnoticed for as long as it did.

Native window - News and Bonuses:
- Merge News and What's New into one "News/What's New" tab, News taking the upper 60%. Both panels are unchanged; they are composed rather than rewritten.
- Add a Bonuses tab showing your fed status and the current food recommendation. The information was already read live, but the full window never had access to it - only the companion window did.
- List every food you are holding, grouped into Combat, Crafting and Gathering by which stats the item actually grants, rather than guessed from its name.
- Rank food within each group using the same cap-first scoring already used to choose the single recommendation, so the tab and the recommendation cannot contradict each other.
- List NQ and HQ of the same item as separate rows, since their bonuses differ, and highlight only the row for the quality you are actually holding.

Recommendations:
- Offer the ten oldest unfinished quests instead of one. The pane it opens into already scrolled and already held a dozen job quests, so nothing new was needed to show them.
- Keep the single quest Classic names unchanged. Ten entries meant deciding what happens when two quests tie on both patch and level; the new ordering was checked against the old one over 20,000 generated cases built to collide often, and the top entry matched every time.
- Cost nothing extra on a new character. The list is built by bounded insertion rather than sorting - on a character with almost nothing complete, sorting five thousand quests to keep ten would throw away 99.8% of the work.
- Add a setting to leave class and job quests out of the shortlist, on by default. Every A Realm Reborn class has an unlock quest at level 1 in patch 2.0, so they tie on both sort keys and could fill all ten slots on a character who has not taken them all.
- Offer it as a setting rather than a filter, because they genuinely are the oldest outstanding quests. Someone working through the classes wants them listed; someone who never intends to wants that corner of the backlog out of the way.
- Match those quests by their English titles, the same method the totals and the export already use, so the setting behaves identically on every client language rather than silently doing nothing.
- Leave the tree, the totals and the export untouched. The setting says what to recommend, not what your character has done.
- Apply the setting immediately. It previously recomputed the shortlist while the screen showed the old one, and only corrected itself when you closed and reopened the window.
- Preserve your scroll position when nothing relevant changed. The list rebuilds when the setting has moved, not on every visit to the tab.
- Hide Recommended entirely under the Done filter. Every quest in it is unfinished by definition, so each branch opened onto blankness rather than saying nothing matched.

Achievement counts:
- Show collectables and duty counts without requiring you to open one specific achievement page first. These came from a single slot holding whichever achievement the client last fetched, so for most characters the three counts simply stayed blank.
- Read them instead from which achievement tiers you have completed, which is available all at once and needs no request to the server.
- Present the result as a guaranteed floor rather than a running total. A completed tier proves you reached its requirement; it cannot tell you how far past it you are.
- Take the reading once per session, since a completed tier cannot become uncompleted.
- Recover the requirement from each achievement's description, because no column in the game's own data holds it.
- Discard an entire achievement series if its parsed requirements do not increase with its tiers. A reworded tier or an unfamiliar language shows up as nonsense ordering, and no figure at all is better than a wrong one presented as a guarantee.
- Name the specific achievement to open in the companion window's hint. The old wording said to open Achievements once, which was wrong - the window can be open and still show nothing.

Adventurer's Ledger export:
- Add thirteen unlock keys the ledger had been approximating from your story patch: a daily key and an elite key for each of the five Hunt boards, plus allied societies, Zodiac and raids.
- Treat the Hunt as five features rather than one. Each expansion has its own board, its own unlock chain and its own weekly elite bill.
- Include Zodiac, previously left out because "A Relic Reborn" is per weapon. The ledger's row is Morbid Motivation, and all thirteen weapon quests converge well before it, so a single quest answers it.
- Keep the existing "eliteHunt" name even though it has always meant the Heavensward chain specifically. Published builds already send it and its value has not changed - only which ledger row should read it was wrong.

Notes:
- New settings arrive with defaults; nothing needs configuring after updating.
- Per-item bag and slot location for food was built and then dropped. The bag reads back correctly, but the inventory window's layout is a client display setting that plugins cannot see, so any "row 3, slot 5" would have been wrong for some players and right for others with no way to tell which.

Something not working, or a figure that looks wrong? Please reach out.

variant.changelog:
Native window improvements: a cleaner News tab, an at-a-glance achievement total, and role-coloured, correctly-ranked food.

News and What's New:
- Merge What's New into the News tab. It was dormant between content patches and had one line to say the rest of the year while permanently holding 40% of the tab's height for it - now it's one continuous panel that only grows a list when there is something to list.
- List up to 60 new quests on a big patch, and say so ("...and N more") rather than silently dropping the rest.

Overview:
- Add an "Achievements" section - "Overall X/Y Z%" - the same grand tally the game's own Achievements window shows, in both Classic and Native.
- Hidden until that window has loaded this login, the same way other totals hide rather than showing a false 0/0.
- Fixes a related gap: switching characters mid-session could silently skip this and other free achievement reads for every character after the first.

Bonuses:
- Colour each held food's stat line by role - Tank, Healer, DPS, Crafter, Gatherer - matching the palette Progression already uses.
- Fix a ranking bug: food was scored by summing every stat's cap regardless of relevance, so a Skill Speed/Direct Hit food could outrank a Piety food for a healer. Ranking now counts only the stats your equipped gear actually uses.
- Rank held food by your real, current stat totals while you are not fed, instead of assuming every food reaches its cap; falls back to the simpler cap-based ranking while fed, since your current total already includes that food's own bonus and multiplying it in again would double-count it.
- Pin the food you are currently eating to the top of its group.

Something not working, or a figure that looks wrong? Please reach out.

variant.author: Legends of the Game
variant.changelog:
Map:
- Click a quest's flag (Native) or its Area column (Classic) to open the game's own map at the spot it's picked up. Classic's version was broken since it first existed -- it passed the wrong coordinate format into the map link, so it never actually opened anywhere.
- A handful of quests sit in interior rooms the game has no map graphic for; those are quietly skipped rather than opening to an error.

Native:
- Maintenance and Active Events now show the same detail Classic always has -- countdowns, start and end times, and a note when a festival is running in game but hasn't reached the news feed yet.

variant.author: Legends of the Game
variant.changelog:
Label: Journal
- Re-baseline: pick a date in Settings, and everything recorded before it is re-marked Pre-Plugin, for when some of those dates are known to be wrong. The journal is backed up first.
- Real completions now record seconds, not just the day, so a bad write leaves an unmistakable shared timestamp instead of an ambiguous busy day.
- Rotating backups: a snapshot before any write, when content actually changed and the newest backup is at least 3 days old. Kept to the newest three.
- A twice-monthly recovery point (1st and 15th of each month), held 32 days, independent of the 3-day rotation.

Label: Interface
- Rewrote the Help tab, wrapped to the actual window width in both Classic and Native.
- Fixed the Progression list overlapping its own footer.
- Raised the Native window's minimum width to 956, growing it live if it was already open narrower.

variant.changelog:
New: /tm <expansion> (arr, hw, sb/stb, shb, ew, dt, ec) opens a list of every unfinished quest in that expansion at once, instead of browsing one category at a time.
- Shows a message instead of a blank list when there's nothing left: congratulations if it's done, or a note that the expansion hasn't released yet.
Fixed: Patch 7.5's Main Scenario finish line now points to the quest 7.56 actually continued the story to (Windborne), not the placeholder set before 7.56 shipped.

variant.author: Legends of the Game
variant.changelog:
Plugin installer:
- The Settings button now opens the window you chose in Settings (Native or Classic), on its Settings tab. Before, it toggled the Classic window on whichever tab was last open.
- The Open button now opens the window you chose, and never closes it if it is already open.

Housekeeping:
- Category metadata is now part of the build itself.
- Unused notification code removed. The plugin never showed toasts or notifications, and still does not.
- README and NOTICE updated. The README now describes the one network request (the News feed). Ocean Fishing: Soon™.

variant.author: Legends of the Game
variant.changelog:
New window:
- /tmwiki opens a small window that lists every quest in your journal. Click a quest to open its page on the FFXIV wiki.
- The quests are grouped by expansion, then by the place headings that the journal uses.
- Click an expansion heading to open the Main Scenario Quests page for that expansion. If you have an MSQ accepted in that expansion, the heading opens the page for the story arc of that quest (for example, Post-Shadowbringers).
- /tmwiki always uses the classic window, also when you chose the Native window in Settings.

Wiki search:
- Some quest names in the game data start with an icon character. The wiki search now removes that character, so the search goes directly to the quest page.

variant.author: Legends of the Game
variant.changelog:
Collections, the bestiary and optional features.
Exports:
- The Ledger export is about half its former size (fmt 2), so it pastes cheaply into other tools. Master recipe books are added.
- New collections export (/tm collections, Copy collections): mounts, minions, orchestrion rolls, Triple Triad cards and NPCs, emotes, fashion accessories, facewear, curiosities, fish, spearfish, Master's Bestiary captures and folklore tomes read.
- World lists in the collections export: sightseeing log, aether currents, aetherytes and porter stops, plus the game client build.
- New full export (/tm full, Copy everything): progress and collections together.
- Quests done, duty clears and quest totals by expansion, so the Ledger can show questlines and a duty grid.
- Mount speed per zone and bicolor gemstones.
Features:
- New Features list in Settings. Each feature is optional and off until you turn it on.
- Master's Bestiary: every Beastmaster beast, where to tame it, the minimum level, the Kornago Gourd, and whether you have captured it. Click Flag to open the map there.
- /bmap turns the Master's Bestiary on and opens it beside the game's own Master's Bestiary. It replaces the Bestiary Mapper plugin.
Fixes:
- Active Events no longer lists an event twice when its name has an apostrophe.
- Levequest folders use the game's job names.

Collections, the bestiary and optional features.

- The Ledger export is about half its former size (fmt 2), so it pastes cheaply into other tools. Master recipe books are added.

- New full export (/tm full, Copy everything): progress and collections together.
- Quests done, duty clears and quest totals by expansion, so the Ledger can show questlines and a duty grid.
- Mount speed per zone and bicolor gemstones.

variant.author: Legends of the Game
variant.changelog:
Relic stages and the Keybound Brawler name.
Exports:
- The collections export (Copy collections, Copy everything) now includes the highest relic stage you hold for each job, from Zodiac to Cosmic Tools. It reads the armoury chest, the bags, the saddlebag, your retainers and the glamour dresser. You do not have to open your retainers: the game's own Search for Item data is used.
Events:
- Active Events shows the Gold Saucer's Keybound Brawler event (festival 257) by name, not as Unknown. The event starts on 28 October 2026 at 08:00 UTC.
Adventurer's Ledger (Pandora Lunar):
- Relics is its own area in the left rail, with one tab for each expansion and the stage of each job's relic.
- Daily, Weekly and Seasonal meters in the rail, events from the Time Memoria news feed, fish and spearfish lists, crafter and gatherer hub quests from 70 to 100.
- Fix: a second open Ledger tab no longer erases changes made in the first tab.

variant.author: Legends of the Game
variant.changelog:
Tales of Milestones:
- Food from your accepted quests. The /tm food window has a new section, "From accepted quests". It lists each quest in your journal that gives food, and the role that each meal suits. A reward that you choose from is under "Pick one:".
- Eye on the quest turn-in window. When a quest reward is food, the turn-in window shows an eye beside "Reward". Click the eye to open /tm food before you choose your reward. The eye opens nothing by itself, and it changes nothing in the game window. To turn it off, use the new setting in either Settings window.
- Text follows your UI theme. The game-styled windows use the text colour of the theme that you selected in the game. Text is now easy to read on the Light, Clear White and Clear Pink themes. Headings are larger. The Bonuses tab shows each food's role as the game's role icon and as a word.
- Language for dates. A new Language setting in both Settings windows selects English, German, French or Japanese. The default follows Dalamud, then the game. Only dates use it at this time.
- News feed date. Active Events shows the time and date when the news feed was last updated, with the month as a name.
- Shorter event names. Active Events shows "Keybound Brawler", not the announcement title "Keybound Brawler Arrives October 28!".
- News checks. The plugin checks the news feed on the feed's own 6-hour schedule: every 15 minutes in the hour after an update, otherwise every 30 minutes.
- Credits. The Credits tab now names skyborn-industries (lodestonenews.com) and aers (FFXIVClientStructs).
- Fix: a meal with no combat stat no longer shows as DPS food. This includes Bacon Broth, the eight resistance Drops, Kingcake and Tailor-made Eel Pie.
- Fix: the download is smaller. The plugin zip no longer contains copies of Dalamud's own files, so it went from 12.7 MB to 1.3 MB.

variant.author: Legends of the Game
variant.changelog:
Tales of Milestones:
- Lucis and Resplendent tools in the export. "Copy collections" and "Copy everything" now include Lucis Tools (Mastercraft, Supra and Lucis) and Resplendent Tools in the relic stages.
- Doman Enclave in the export. The export now says when you finished Lighting the Way, the quest that ends Doman Enclave Reconstruction.
Adventurer's Ledger (Pandora Lunar):
- Fix: the Relics area counts weapons and tools. The Relics overview counted relic quests, so a row could show as complete when you held no weapon from that line. The area now has Weapons and Tools tabs, with one panel for each relic line. Each panel shows the number complete, for example "1 of 102 Complete", and opens to a grid of stages and jobs. A held stage also counts the stages before it. The rail meter counts weapons.
- Relic quests moved. The relic quest counts are now in Story, under Questlines.
- Lucis and Resplendent tools. The Tools tab has panels for these two lines. To fill them, update Tales of Milestones to this version and import a new export. Until you do this, the two panels show 0.
- Doman Enclave. After Lighting the Way, the Doman Enclave row shows as optional. The weekly meter and the import's feature count leave it out.
- Challenges menu. The site bar has a Challenges menu with Apex Legends and a link to request a game.
- Fix: the aether current total no longer counts retired currents. The total is now 303, not 448.

- Lucis and Resplendent tools in the export. "Copy collections" and "Copy everything" now include Lucis Tools (Mastercraft, Supra and Lucis) and Resplendent Tools in the relic stages.
- Doman Enclave in the export. The export now says when you finished Lighting the Way, the quest that ends Doman Enclave Reconstruction.
Adventurer's Ledger (Pandora Lunar):
- Fix: the Relics area counts weapons and tools. The Relics overview counted relic quests, so a row could show as complete when you held no weapon from that line. The area now has Weapons and Tools tabs, with one panel for each relic line. Each panel shows the number complete, for example "1 of 102 Complete", and opens to a grid of stages and jobs. A held stage also counts the stages before it. The rail meter counts weapons.
- Relic quests moved. The relic quest counts are now in Story, under Questlines.
- Lucis and Resplendent tools. The Tools tab has panels for these two lines. To fill them, update Tales of Milestones to this version and import a new export. Until you do this, the two panels show 0.
- Doman Enclave. After Lighting the Way, the Doman Enclave row shows as optional. The weekly meter and the import's feature count leave it out.
- Challenges menu. The site bar has a Challenges menu with Apex Legends and a link to request a game.
- Fix: the aether current total no longer counts retired currents. The total is now 303, not 448.
variant.description: Quest progression and pacing — a reflective notebook for your story journey, not a scoreboard.
variant.name: Tales of Milestones

variant.author: Legends of the Game
variant.changelog:
Tales of Milestones:
- Eat buttons on the Bonuses tab. Each meal in your inventory has an Eat button. One click eats one meal. The button is not available when the game refuses the meal.
- Eat button in /tm food. The food window has the same button for a meal that is in your inventory.
- /tm eat. `/tm eat dps`, `tank`, `healer`, `battle`, `craft`, `gather` or `all` eats your meal of that kind when you hold only one such meal. When you hold more than one, the Bonuses tab opens and you select the meal.
- Playtime in the export. The export adds the time that the plugin recorded after your last `/playtime` reply, so the playtime is current at the time of the export. The plugin does not run `/playtime`.
- Armor, GARO and more weapons in the export. "Copy collections" and "Copy everything" now include relic armor, GARO gear, and the Figmental, Exquisite and Deep Dungeon weapons.
- The native windows use less processor time. The at-a-glance window and the tabs of the main window now update one time each second, not on each frame. In a test, the at-a-glance window changed from about 1.2 ms to about 0.08 ms for each frame.
- Fix: the plugin no longer writes its settings file every 5 seconds while Cosmic Exploration data is loaded. It writes the file only when a tool's progress changes.
- Fix: the job list on the Progression tab no longer scrolls past its end.
- KamiToolKit is updated to its current version.
Adventurer's Ledger (Pandora Lunar):
- New layout. Next Steps is the first screen. It shows 5 cards for what to do next, and "Show 5 more" shows 10. Daily, Weekly and Seasonal rows are below it in the rail. The header shows the area title, the age of your data and 4 clocks.
- Challenge Log. Each Challenge Log entry has its own row, with links and typed counts. Suggested and Completed groups are included.
- Routine sub-checks. A routine can have its own boxes: one for each roulette, a Tank You pick, 12 allied society boxes and Grand Company chips. "Edit routines" changes the rows.
- Relics by job. The Relics area has a By job view and line cards with progress bars. To fill the Armor and GARO frames, update Tales of Milestones to this version and import a new export.
- Societies, currents and collections. Societies show unlock lines and rank bars. Aether currents are listed by zone. Collections are grouped by availability, with Online Store links.
- Settings area. Character, display, and backup and import settings are in one area. The Ledger holds up to 8 characters, and times can show in UTC or local time.
- Themes. The three themes are Lunar night, Crystarium and Light. Expansion tags use the colours of the Lodestone patch notes.
- Jobs meter. The rail has a Jobs meter that adds your combat, crafting and gathering levels, out of 3,330.
- Fix: after an import, the relic row in the list of changes counts relic items. Before, a stage upgrade showed no change, for example "9 to 9".

variant.author: Legends of the Game
variant.changelog:
Tales of Milestones:
- Hunt group counts. The export now carries the game's count for each of the 16 A and S rank "Mark of the ..." achievements (A Realm Reborn, Heavensward and Stormblood). A finished group is read when the Achievements window loads. The count is for the group only. The plugin does not record which mark you killed.
- Read hunt counts. A new button on the Progression tab, in both windows, asks the game for all 16 counts, one at a time (about 10 seconds). It runs only when you press it. It is the only request that the plugin sends to the game server.
- /tmwiki: allied society quests and levequests. Allied society quests are in their own group under each expansion, with one heading for each society. Held levequests are listed in their own section, grouped by town. Each one opens its wiki page.
- Food location on the Bonuses tab. Each food row shows where the food is: B1 to B4 for the inventory block (the same number as /isearch), and S for the saddlebag.
- Journal re-baseline in the native window. The Settings tab of the native window can now re-baseline the journal, as the classic window can. Click Set Baseline, then click again within 5 seconds to confirm.
- Lodestone links in the native window. Maintenance and Active Events rows have a Read button after the title. It opens the Lodestone page.
- Ko-fi heart. The classic main window has a heart in its title bar. A click opens the Ko-fi page. It is a link only.
- Main Scenario pacing. The Main Scenario rate stops at the final Main Scenario quest, so play after it does not change the rate. The classic window now shows the Main Scenario row too.
- Adventurer's Ledger link. "Open Adventurer's Ledger" now opens legendmemoria.org/lunar.
- Keybound Brawler end date. The news feed now gives Keybound Brawler's end, the release of Patch 8.0, so Active Events shows when it ends.
- Fix: the FINAL FANTASY XVI crossover, The Path Infernal, showed twice in Active Events, once as "Festival #147". It now shows once, with its name.
- The AI declaration is corrected and complete, and "tracker" is removed from the plugin's tags.
Adventurer's Ledger (Pandora Lunar):
- Hunt counts on the Hunts tab. After an import from this version, each A and S rank group shows the game's count beside your ticks, for example "The game counts 5 of 6; you have ticked 4". It never ticks anything.
- Armor cards. The Armor frame shows one card for each armor set, with "3 of 5 slots" for each role or job that holds a piece. The full grid is inside each card.
- GARO weapon card. The GARO frame shows the GARO weapons as a line card, like Weapons and Tools. The GARO armor grid is below it.
- Where a relic line starts. When the starting quest of a relic line is not open yet, the card names the first quest to do on the way to it.
- Custom Deliveries boxes. The Custom Deliveries routine has 12 boxes, one for each weekly delivery. Each box also counts for The Customer Is Always Right in the Challenge Log.
- Weekly meter. The Weekly meter now counts Challenge Log entries that you completed in the last 4 weeks, beside your weekly routines.
- Crafting solver. The Jobs area has a crafting solver that finds a rotation for one recipe. It is built from Raphael (Apache-2.0) and runs in your browser.
- Moved notice. The old github.io address shows a notice that the Ledger has moved, with a Download backup button.
- Fix: the Seasonal meter read the FINAL FANTASY XVI crossover as the FINAL FANTASY XV one and counted the wrong quests.

A finished group is read when the Achievements window loads. The count is for the group only. The plugin does not record which mark you killed.
- Read hunt counts. A new button on the Progression tab, in both windows, asks the game for all 16 counts, one at a time (about 10 seconds). It runs only when you press it. It is the only request that the plugin sends to the game server.

- Journal re-baseline in the native window. The Settings tab of the native window can now re-baseline the journal, as the classic window can. Click Set Baseline, then click again within 5 seconds to confirm.
- Lodestone links in the native window. Maintenance and Active Events rows have a Read button after the title. It opens the Lodestone page.
- Ko-fi heart. The classic main window has a heart in its title bar. A click opens the Ko-fi page. It is a link only.
- Main Scenario pacing. The Main Scenario rate stops at the final Main Scenario quest, so play after it does not change the rate. The classic window now shows the Main Scenario row too.
- Adventurer's Ledger link. "Open Adventurer's Ledger" now opens legendmemoria.org/lunar.
- Keybound Brawler end date. The news feed now gives Keybound Brawler's end, the release of Patch 8.0, so Active Events shows when it ends.

- Hunt counts on the Hunts tab. After an import from this version, each A and S rank group shows the game's count beside your ticks, for example "The game counts 5 of 6; you have ticked 4". It never ticks anything.

- GARO weapon card. The GARO frame shows the GARO weapons as a line card, like Weapons and Tools. The GARO armor grid is below it.
- Where a relic line starts. When the starting quest of a relic line is not open yet, the card names the first quest to do on the way to it.

- Crafting solver. The Jobs area has a crafting solver that finds a rotation for one recipe. It is built from Raphael (Apache-2.0) and runs in your browser.
- Moved notice. The old github.io address shows a notice that the Ledger has moved, with a Download backup button.
- Fix: the Seasonal meter read the FINAL FANTASY XVI crossover as the FINAL FANTASY XV one and counted the wrong quests.

variant.author: Legends of the Game
variant.changelog:
Tales of Milestones:
- Smaller export (format 3). Every id list in the export now writes a run of three or more consecutive ids as a pair, for example `[1700,1708]` for 1700 to 1708. A full export is about half its old size, so it is quicker to paste into the Ledger or into an AI. The data in the export is the same. The Adventurer's Ledger reads format 3 already, and exports from older versions still import.
Adventurer's Ledger (Pandora Lunar):
- Share codes. Settings has a Share frame. It makes a short code, for example `K7Q2-M9XP`, for one character. Anyone with the code can open a read-only view of that character's progress. A code expires 48 hours after the last share, unless you tick "Keep this code permanently".
- Backup with a share code. Each share also stores that character's ticks, notes and display settings as a backup. Your browser encrypts the backup before it goes up, and only your owner key or one of your one-time recovery codes can open it. Use the owner key or a recovery code to restore the character in another browser. Keep them safe: if you lose both, make a new share with a new code.
- Permanent codes update by themselves. After you save a change, a permanent code uploads it again about a minute later, at most once every 15 minutes, while a Ledger page is open. The Share frame shows when the next automatic update goes up. Timed codes update only when you share again.
- Format 3 imports. The Ledger imports exports in the new, smaller format, and exports in the earlier formats.
- Challenge Log tab. The completion percentage updates on each + or − click, and the categories are in the same order as in the game.

variant.changelog:
Tales of Milestones:
- Hunting Log window (`/hunt`). A new optional feature. Type `/hunt`, or switch it on in Settings. The window shows every Hunting Log monster that you still need, for all your unlocked classes and your Grand Company at the same time. You do not have to change class to see a class's log. Each row shows the class, the task, the monster, your kills and where to find it. Finished monsters, finished ranks and locked classes are not shown.
- Map flags for Hunting Log monsters. Click Flag on a row to open the map at that monster. If the monster is also in your current zone, the row shows that location. The locations come from the Hunty plugin by Infiziert90 (MIT License).
- Current class only and Current zone only. Two check boxes in the Hunting Log window. With Current zone only, the window shows only the monsters in the zone where you are, for all classes. The window updates when you change class or zone.
- Change class from the Hunting Log. In the summary line at the top of the window, click a class name to equip a gear set for that class. If you have more than one gear set for the class, a list opens and you select one. The game's own Gear Set function does the change, the same as a click in the Gear Set window. Nothing is sent to chat.
- Hunting Log in the export. The export has a new `huntLog` block with each class's rank and kill counts. The Adventurer's Ledger reads it.
- Leve markers. In the quest list, a leve whose items are in your bags now shows "[R]" in place of a check mark. The check mark means "complete" in the News panel. Hold the pointer on a leve row to see what "> " and "[R]" mean.
- Fix: allied societies in the mini window. The society list shows only societies that are capped and wait for a main quest. Societies at their last rank are not listed.
Adventurer's Ledger (Pandora Lunar):
- Hunting Log. Jobs has a Hunting Log frame. It shows each class's rank, its tasks complete, and the monsters it still needs, with the place. Import a Tales of Milestones export to fill it in.
- Gear guide. Jobs has a Gear guide frame. Select one job and level. It shows the highest item level for each slot from the sources that you tick, with options for your export, crafting, NPC vendors and the market board.
- Mentor Roulette readiness. The Mentor tab has a Roulette frame, also listed under Jobs and Duties. It shows the Battle Mentor requirements: the level 100 role quests, a combat job at level 100, and each duty in the game's Mentor Roulette pool cleared once. Missing duties are listed by expansion and type. Item level 755 is a manual check, because the export does not have it.
- Import preview: Challenge Log. When an export opens new Challenge Log entries, the import preview shows them, for example "Challenge Log entries open: 40 → 41 (new: Soul Survivor I)".
- Allied societies. When every society in a group is at its last rank and the Intersocietal Quests are done, the group shows only the names, ranks and the quest check box.
- Fix: Ocean Fishing clock. The bar shows the time as "29:58" again, not "00:29:58".
- Fix: new characters. A new character no longer stops the Quest items frame after you enter a crafter or gatherer level. "Mark items HQ" is on by default again.
- Fix: backup import. A backup with no characters no longer leaves the page empty until a reload.
- Fix: Challenge Log. The Challenge Log list now comes from the game's data, so it matches the game after a patch.
- Fix: smaller items. The Collections filter (All, Owned, Missing) keeps its selection when you change area. Collapsed sections stay collapsed. Ended events leave the events feed. The time zone and hunt switches work with Space and Enter.
- Faster pages. The Ledger draws only the area and frame on screen.

variant.author: Legends of the Game
variant.changelog:
Tales of Milestones:
- Read achievement counts. This button replaces "Read hunt counts" on the Progression tab, in both windows. It asks the game for 19 counts, one at a time (about 12 seconds): gathered collectables, crafted collectables, duties, and the 16 A and S rank hunt groups. You do not have to open the Achievements window first. It runs only when you press it.
- Read counts, copy everything. A new button. It reads the same 19 counts, then copies the full export when the read ends. This button and "Read achievement counts" send the only requests that the plugin sends to the game server.
- Age of the counts. The plugin shows when you last read the counts: beside the button in the classic window, and in the button's tooltip in the native window. "Copy for Adventurer's Ledger", "Copy everything", `/tm ledger` and `/tm full` also say it, for example "Achievement counts: 19 of 19, 3d ago."
- Copy collections button removed. "Copy everything" includes the collections. The command `/tm collections` stays.
- Gear rewards at the turn-in. When a reward option is gear, the quest turn-in window shows the eye beside "Reward". Click it to open `/tm food`, which shows how each option changes the bonuses that your current class uses. The option with the largest total gain is marked "Most improved".
- Smaller hunt groups in the export. The export no longer repeats each hunt group's name. The Adventurer's Ledger uses the id.
- Fix: old collectable and duty counts. A newer reading of an earlier tier could be ignored in favour of an older reading of a later tier, so a count could stay too low. The higher count now stays, whatever tier it came from.
- Fix: reading times. After a plugin reload, the last achievement read is no longer given a new time.
- Fix: long food names. In `/tm food`, a long name no longer covers the text on its right.
Adventurer's Ledger (Pandora Lunar):
- Relic grids. The relic grids show each row in its tier colour, as the stage bar does. The Cosmic and Eureka grids count every stage (220 and 240).
- Fix: relic cards. A relic card that has a starting quest no longer says "no starting quest".
- Fix: job tables. The "not levelled" note counts only the jobs in its own table and shows only in that table's frame.

It asks the game for 19 counts, one at a time (about 12 seconds): gathered collectables, crafted collectables, duties, and the 16 A and S rank hunt groups. You do not have to open the Achievements window first. It runs only when you press it.
- Read counts, copy everything. A new button. It reads the same 19 counts, then copies the full export when the read ends. This button and "Read achievement counts" send the only requests that the plugin sends to the game server.
- Age of the counts. The plugin shows when you last read the counts: beside the button in the classic window, and in the button's tooltip in the native window. "Copy for Adventurer's Ledger", "Copy everything", `/tm ledger` and `/tm full` also say it, for example "Achievement counts: 19 of 19, 3d ago."
- Copy collections button removed. "Copy everything" includes the collections. The command `/tm collections` stays.
- Gear rewards at the turn-in. When a reward option is gear, the quest turn-in window shows the eye beside "Reward". Click it to open `/tm food`, which shows how each option changes the bonuses that your current class uses. The option with the largest total gain is marked "Most improved".
- Smaller hunt groups in the export. The export no longer repeats each hunt group's name. The Adventurer's Ledger uses the id.
- Fix: old collectable and duty counts. A newer reading of an earlier tier could be ignored in favour of an older reading of a later tier, so a count could stay too low. The higher count now stays, whatever tier it came from.
- Fix: reading times. After a plugin reload, the last achievement read is no longer given a new time.
- Fix: long food names. In `/tm food`, a long name no longer covers the text on its right.
Adventurer's Ledger (Pandora Lunar):
- Relic grids. The relic grids show each row in its tier colour, as the stage bar does. The Cosmic and Eureka grids count every stage (220 and 240).
- Fix: relic cards. A relic card that has a starting quest no longer says "no starting quest".
- Fix: job tables. The "not levelled" note counts only the jobs in its own table and shows only in that table's frame.

- Smaller hunt groups in the export. The export no longer repeats each hunt group's name. The Adventurer's Ledger uses the id.
- Fix: old collectable and duty counts. A newer reading of an earlier tier could be ignored in favour of an older reading of a later tier, so a count could stay too low. The higher count now stays, whatever tier it came from.

- Fix: long food names. In `/tm food`, a long name no longer covers the text on its right.

- Relic grids. The relic grids show each row in its tier colour, as the stage bar does. The Cosmic and Eureka grids count every stage (220 and 240).
- Fix: relic cards. A relic card that has a starting quest no longer says "no starting quest".
- Fix: job tables. The "not levelled" note counts only the jobs in its own table and shows only in that table's frame.
